221	    @staticmethod
222	    def _decode_lines(data):
223	        # Split the raw JSONL bytes into physical lines while treating the
224	        # first illegal UTF-8 byte as a hard, locatable stop point.
225	        # Returns (lines, bad_line): lines are the complete physical lines
226	        # preceding any corruption (all lines when the file is valid UTF-8),
227	        # bad_line is the 1-based line number of the first undecodable line
228	        # or None. A bad line is never yielded, even if the bytes before the
229	        # illegal byte looked like complete JSON: callers scan the preceding
230	        # complete lines first, so an earlier JSON/sequence/digest error
231	        # still takes priority.
232	        try:
233	            return data.decode("utf-8").splitlines(), None
234	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
235	            # start is the offset of the first byte that cannot be decoded;
236	            # everything before it is a valid UTF-8 prefix.
237	            start = exc.start
238	        bad_line = data.count(b"\n", 0, start) + 1
239	        cut = data.rfind(b"\n", 0, start) + 1  # start of the bad line
240	        return data[:cut].decode("utf-8").splitlines(), bad_line
241	
242	    @staticmethod
243	    def _tenant_key(tenant):
244	        # Canonical JSON data identity of a tenant value. Object key order is
245	        # normalized away, while distinct JSON types or number spellings stay
246	        # distinct partitions: 1, 1.0, true and "1" are four different
247	        # tenants regardless of host-language loose equality.
248	        return json.dumps(tenant, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
249	
250	    @staticmethod
251	    def _hash(item):
252	        payload = json.dumps(
253	            {k: item[k] for k in ("tenant", "seq", "event", "prev")},
254	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
255	        )
256	        return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
257	
258	    def _scan(self, tenant, lines, bad_line=None):
259	        # Validate the target tenant's chain over the decoded JSONL lines.
260	        # Returns (verified_count, last_hash). Raises _Broken at the first
261	        # problem; records of other tenants may interleave and are skipped.
262	        # Tenant matching uses the same canonical JSON identity as
263	        # verify_all, never host-language loose equality. If bad_line is
264	        # given, an undecodable physical line follows the lines provided;
265	        # it is reported as missing only when no earlier problem was found.
266	        key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
267	        expected, prev, count = 1, ZERO, 0
268	        for line, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):
269	            try:
270	                item = _strict_loads(raw)
271	            except Exception:
272	                raise _Broken("missing", None, line, expected)
273	            if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
274	                raise _Broken("missing", None, line, expected)
275	            if self._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) != key:
276	                continue
277	            if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
278	                seq = item.get("seq")
279	                at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) and not isinstance(seq, bool) else None
280	                raise _Broken("missing", at, line, expected)
281	            if isinstance(item["seq"], bool) or item["seq"] != expected:
282	                raise _Broken("sequence", expected, line, expected)
283	            if item["prev"] != prev:
284	                raise _Broken("digest", expected, line, expected)
285	            if item["hash"] != self._hash(item):
286	                raise _Broken("digest", expected, line, expected)
287	            count += 1
288	            prev = item["hash"]
289	            expected += 1
290	        if bad_line is not None:
291	            raise _Broken("missing", None, bad_line, expected)
292	        return count, prev
293	
294	    def _scan_import(self, tenant, lines, bad_line=None):
295	        # Validate an offline single-tenant export before it is grafted onto
296	        # another log. Unlike _scan, no foreign records are tolerated: every
297	        # physical line must be a well-formed record carrying the exact same
298	        # canonical JSON tenant identity, seqs must run 1..n from a ZERO prev,
299	        # and each digest must verify. Returns the parsed records in physical
300	        # (== seq) order. A chain defect raises _Broken with the same
301	        # reason/at/line/expect filling rules _scan uses, so the resulting
302	        # AuditChainStateError is shaped exactly like append's; a record of
303	        # another tenant identity violates the single-tenant input contract
304	        # and raises _ForeignTenant (surfaced as ValueError by import_tenant),
305	        # with the first problem in physical order taking priority.
306	        key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
307	        records = []
308	        expected, prev = 1, ZERO
309	        for line, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):
310	            try:
311	                item = _strict_loads(raw)
312	            except Exception:
313	                raise _Broken("missing", None, line, expected)
314	            if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
315	                raise _Broken("missing", None, line, expected)
316	            if self._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) != key:
317	                raise _ForeignTenant(line)
318	            if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
319	                seq = item.get("seq")
320	                at = seq if isinstance(seq, int) and not isinstance(seq, bool) else None
321	                raise _Broken("missing", at, line, expected)
322	            if isinstance(item["seq"], bool) or item["seq"] != expected:
323	                raise _Broken("sequence", expected, line, expected)
324	            if item["prev"] != prev:
325	                raise _Broken("digest", expected, line, expected)
326	            if item["hash"] != self._hash(item):
327	                raise _Broken("digest", expected, line, expected)
328	            records.append(item)
329	            prev = item["hash"]
330	            expected += 1
331	        if bad_line is not None:
332	            raise _Broken("missing", None, bad_line, expected)
333	        return records
334	
335	    def append(self, tenant, event):
336	        # Validate the new input against the standard-JSON boundary before
337	        # anything else: an illegal tenant/event raises ValueError without
338	        # reading history or writing a single byte, and takes priority over
339	        # any append action (including corrupt-history rejection). It is
340	        # deliberately also evaluated before taking the lock, so a malformed
341	        # caller can never be turned into a different outcome by contention.
342	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
343	        _validate_json_value(event)
344	        with self._write_lease() as f:
345	            # The scan and the write happen under one exclusive lease on the
346	            # very file description used for both, so the record is always
347	            # computed from the latest complete state right before its own
348	            # bytes hit disk: competing appends serialize here and each
349	            # observes the previous winner's record already on disk.
350	            data = f.read()
351	            lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
352	            try:
353	                count, prev = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
354	            except _Broken as b:
355	                seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
356	                raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
357	            item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1, "event": event, "prev": prev}
358	            item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
359	            # One O_APPEND write places the whole record atomically at the
360	            # current end of the file; under the exclusive lease no other
361	            # writer moves that end, and no existing byte can be overwritten.
362	            prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
363	            record = prefix + (
364	                json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
365	            ).encode("utf-8")
366	            f.write(record)
367	            return item
368	
369	    def append_batch(self, tenant, events):
370	        # Append a group of same-tenant events as one verifiable interval.
371	        # events must be a list (a bare JSON value, including a string, is
372	        # not a batch); the tenant and every event cross the same standard-
373	        # JSON boundary as in append. All of this is checked before taking
374	        # the lease, so a malformed call raises ValueError without reading
375	        # history or creating the file, under any contention. An empty list
376	        # is a no-op: nothing is created and no existing byte is touched.
377	        if not isinstance(events, list):
378	            raise ValueError(
379	                f"events must be a list, got {type(events).__name__}"
380	            )
381	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
382	        for event in events:
383	            _validate_json_value(event)
384	        if not events:
385	            return []
386	        with self._write_lease() as f:
387	            # One lease covers the whole read-build-append interval, so the
388	            # batch is an indivisible result for competing writers: their
389	            # records serialize wholly before or wholly after these, never
390	            # between two of its records. The records are emitted as one
391	            # byte block at the current end of file, so readers under the
392	            # shared lease likewise see either the whole batch or none of
393	            # it. The first record continues the tenant chain found on disk;
394	            # each later record links to the previous record of the batch.
395	            data = f.read()
396	            lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
397	            try:
398	                count, prev = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
399	            except _Broken as b:
400	                seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
401	                raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
402	            items = []
403	            chunks = []
404	            for event in events:
405	                item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1,
406	                        "event": event, "prev": prev}
407	                item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
408	                items.append(item)
409	                chunks.append(
410	                    json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
411	                )
412	                count += 1
413	                prev = item["hash"]
414	            prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
415	            block = prefix + "".join(chunks).encode("utf-8")
416	            f.write(block)
417	            return items
418	
419	    def _append_batch_if_head_locked(self, f, tenant, events,
420	                                     expected_count, expected_hash):
421	        # Scan, compare and append on a description already holding the
422	        # exclusive data-file lease. A corrupt history is reported exactly as
423	        # append reports it and the assertion is never evaluated against an
424	        # unverifiable chain; a well-formed but mismatching head is a conflict.
425	        # Nothing is written on either failure path.
426	        data = f.read()
427	        lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
428	        try:
429	            count, head = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
430	        except _Broken as b:
431	            seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
432	            raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
433	        # _scan returns ZERO for an empty chain, so an empty history is
434	        # compared by the exact same rule as a non-empty one: the call
435	        # proceeds only when both the length and the tail digest match.
436	        if count != expected_count or head != expected_hash:
437	            raise AuditChainConflictError(
438	                tenant, expected_count, expected_hash, count, head
439	            )
440	        # Head confirmed. The records use the identical fields, seq numbering,
441	        # prev digest and hash algorithm as append: the first continues the
442	        # asserted chain head, each later one links to the previous record of
443	        # the batch, exactly as append_batch links its records.
444	        items = []
445	        chunks = []
446	        prev = head
447	        for event in events:
448	            item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1,
449	                    "event": event, "prev": prev}
450	            item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
451	            items.append(item)
452	            chunks.append(
453	                json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
454	            )
455	            count += 1
456	            prev = item["hash"]

458	        # current end of file; under the exclusive lease no other writer
459	        # moves that end, and no existing byte can be overwritten.
460	        prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
461	        block = prefix + "".join(chunks).encode("utf-8")

474	    @contextlib.contextmanager
475	    def _head_lease(self, tenant, expected_count, expected_hash):
476	        # One exclusive lease covering validation-read, head comparison and
477	        # the write of a conditional append. On an existing log that is the
478	        # ordinary data-file lease; before the log exists, the data-file lock
479	        # cannot be taken without creating the path (and a losing assertion
480	        # must leave no file), so the directory lease -- the same one ordinary
481	        # appends hold while creating the file -- guards the whole
482	        # missing-file branch. The existence probe, the empty-chain
483	        # comparison and a winning creation are therefore indivisible
484	        # relative to every other writer. Lock order is always
485	        # directory-then-data, so the nesting cannot deadlock against a plain
486	        # append. _dir_lease also ensures the parent directory exists.
487	        with self._dir_lease():
488	            try:
489	                f = open(self.path, "r+b")
490	            except FileNotFoundError:
491	                # Definitive empty chain for every tenant: no other writer
492	                # can create the path while this lease is held. A non-empty
493	                # assertion is a deterministic conflict and must not create
494	                # the log; only an exact (0, ZERO) assertion may.
495	                if expected_count != 0 or expected_hash != ZERO:
496	                    raise AuditChainConflictError(
497	                        tenant, expected_count, expected_hash, 0, ZERO
498	                    )
499	                f = open(self.path, "a+b")
500	            try:
501	                fcntl.flock(f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
502	                f.seek(0)
503	                # When the file existed, assertions against the same head
504	                # serialize here: one appends and observes (count, head),
505	                # every other observes the winner's new tail and gets the
506	                # conflict with the actual values, no byte written by a
507	                # losing call. When this call just created the file the scan
508	                # confirms the empty head it was allowed to create for.
509	                yield f
510	            finally:
511	                f.flush()
512	                f.close()

524	        # branch) is shared with append_batch_if_head; see _head_lease.

534	    def append_batch_if_head(self, tenant, events,
535	                             expected_count, expected_hash):
536	        # Conditional batch append: append_batch's atomic group commit fused
537	        # with append_if_head's optimistic head assertion. events must be a
538	        # list (a bare JSON value, including a string, is not a batch); the
539	        # tenant and every event cross the same standard-JSON boundary as
540	        # append; expected_count must be a non-negative plain int (bool,
541	        # negative, float and other types are ValueError) and expected_hash
542	        # must be exactly the 64 lowercase hex characters of a sha256 digest
543	        # (the empty-chain head is asserted with ZERO). Every input crosses
544	        # its boundary before a lease is taken, a path is probed or a single
545	        # byte is read, so a malformed call raises ValueError without
546	        # creating or touching anything, under any contention. An empty list
547	        # is a no-op after validation: nothing is created, no existing byte
548	        # is touched and no assertion is evaluated.
549	        if not isinstance(events, list):
550	            raise ValueError(
551	                f"events must be a list, got {type(events).__name__}"
552	            )
553	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
554	        for event in events:
555	            _validate_json_value(event)
556	        _validate_required_count(expected_count)
557	        _validate_expected_hash(expected_hash)
558	        if not events:
559	            return []
560	        # One exclusive lease covers the scan of the tenant's full chain, the
561	        # head comparison and the single block write, so the batch commits as
562	        # one indivisible byte interval: competing writers and shared-lease
563	        # readers only ever observe the state wholly before or wholly after
564	        # it. A corrupt history raises AuditChainStateError (same
565	        # tenant/seq/reason/line as append) and takes priority over the
566	        # conflict check; a well-formed but mismatching head raises
567	        # AuditChainConflictError with the actual tail; neither failure path
568	        # writes a byte. On a not-yet-existing log only an exact (0, ZERO)
569	        # assertion may create the file (see _head_lease). The returned
570	        # records are numbered from expected_count + 1 with the first prev
571	        # equal to expected_hash, and the committed bytes are identical to
572	        # calling append for each event in order from the same head.
573	        with self._head_lease(tenant, expected_count, expected_hash) as f:
574	            return self._append_batch_if_head_locked(
575	                f, tenant, events, expected_count, expected_hash
576	            )

578	    def append_many(self, entries):
579	        # Cross-tenant atomic append. entries must be a list of objects whose
580	        # key set is exactly {"tenant", "event"}; list order is the write
581	        # order. All of that, plus the standard-JSON boundary on every tenant
582	        # and event, is checked before a lease is taken, a path is probed or a
583	        # single byte is read, so a malformed call raises ValueError without
584	        # creating or touching anything, under any contention. An empty list
585	        # is a no-op after validation: no file is created, no history is read
586	        # and no byte changes.
587	        if not isinstance(entries, list):
588	            raise ValueError(
589	                f"entries must be a list, got {type(entries).__name__}"
590	            )
591	        norm = []
592	        for entry in entries:
593	            if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"tenant", "event"}:
594	                raise ValueError(
595	                    "each entry must be an object containing exactly the "
596	                    f"keys 'tenant' and 'event', got {entry!r}"
597	                )
598	            tenant, event = entry["tenant"], entry["event"]
599	            _validate_json_value(tenant)
600	            _validate_json_value(event)
601	            norm.append((tenant, event))
602	        if not norm:
603	            return []
604	        with self._write_lease() as f:
605	            # One lease and one consistent snapshot cover the validation of
606	            # every affected chain and the single block write, so the whole
607	            # group commits as one indivisible byte interval: competing
608	            # writers serialize wholly before or after it and shared-lease
609	            # readers observe either the complete pre-commit or the complete
610	            # post-commit state, never a partial group.
611	            data = f.read()
612	            lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
613	            # Each involved tenant gets the exact full-chain scan append
614	            # runs (seqs 1..n from a ZERO prev, each digest recomputed);
615	            # foreign records interleave freely. A defect is recorded, not
616	            # raised immediately: when several affected chains are broken,
617	            # the first physical line in the log decides the result, and an
618	            # equal line is broken by input order.
619	            heads = {}   # serialized tenant -> [count, prev]
620	            broken = []  # (line, first_input_index, AuditChainStateError)
621	            for idx, (tenant, _event) in enumerate(norm):
622	                key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
623	                if key in heads:
624	                    continue
625	                try:
626	                    count, prev = self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
627	                except _Broken as b:
628	                    seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
629	                    broken.append((
630	                        b.line, idx,
631	                        AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line),
632	                    ))
633	                else:
634	                    heads[key] = [count, prev]
635	            if broken:
636	                raise min(broken, key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))[2] from None
637	            # Every affected pre-state is valid. Build the records in input
638	            # order; a tenant appearing several times gets contiguous seq
639	            # numbering for its occurrences, each record linking to the
640	            # previous one (on disk or earlier in this group), using the
641	            # identical fields, seq numbering, prev digest and hash rule as
642	            # append.
643	            items = []
644	            chunks = []
645	            progress = {key: [count, prev] for key, (count, prev) in heads.items()}
646	            for tenant, event in norm:
647	                key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
648	                count, prev = progress[key]
649	                item = {"tenant": tenant, "seq": count + 1,
650	                        "event": event, "prev": prev}
651	                item["hash"] = self._hash(item)
652	                items.append(item)
653	                chunks.append(
654	                    json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
655	                )
656	                progress[key] = [count + 1, item["hash"]]
657	            # One O_APPEND write places the whole group atomically at the
658	            # current end of file; under the exclusive lease no other writer
659	            # moves that end, and no existing byte can be overwritten. The
660	            # physical JSONL order is the input order, while other tenants'
661	            # legitimate interleaved records already on disk stay in place.
662	            prefix = b"" if (not data or data.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
663	            f.write(prefix + "".join(chunks).encode("utf-8"))
664	            return items

666	    def _verify_all_snapshot(self, data):
667	        # Core of verify_all over an exact in-memory snapshot. Touches no path:
668	        # the caller owns how the bytes were obtained (a shared-lease file read
669	        # or a caller-supplied buffer), so the same logic backs both
670	        # verify_all and the offline verify_all_bytes entry point.
671	        lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
672	        states = {}  # serialized tenant -> [expected_seq, prev_hash, count]
673	        order = []   # (tenant_value, state) in first-appearance order
674	        for line, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):
675	            try:
676	                item = _strict_loads(raw)
677	            except Exception:
678	                return {"ok": False, "at": line, "tenant": None, "reason": "missing"}
679	            if not isinstance(item, dict) or "tenant" not in item:
680	                return {"ok": False, "at": line, "tenant": None, "reason": "missing"}
681	            tenant = item["tenant"]
682	            if any(k not in item for k in FIELDS):
683	                return {"ok": False, "at": line, "tenant": tenant, "reason": "missing"}
684	            key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
685	            state = states.get(key)
686	            if state is None:
687	                state = [1, ZERO, 0]
688	                states[key] = state
689	                order.append((tenant, state))
690	            expected, prev, _ = state
691	            if isinstance(item["seq"], bool) or item["seq"] != expected:
692	                return {"ok": False, "at": line, "tenant": tenant, "reason": "sequence"}
693	            if item["prev"] != prev:
694	                return {"ok": False, "at": line, "tenant": tenant, "reason": "digest"}
695	            if item["hash"] != self._hash(item):
696	                return {"ok": False, "at": line, "tenant": tenant, "reason": "digest"}
697	            state[0] += 1
698	            state[1] = item["hash"]
699	            state[2] += 1
700	        if bad_line is not None:
701	            # First undecodable byte: tenant cannot be parsed, so None.
702	            return {"ok": False, "at": bad_line, "tenant": None, "reason": "missing"}
703	        return {"ok": True,
704	                "tenants": [{"tenant": t, "count": s[2]} for t, s in order]}

706	    def verify_all(self):
707	        # Validate every tenant chain in one read-only pass over the file, in
708	        # physical line order. Each tenant gets an independent expected seq and
709	        # prev digest starting at (1, ZERO) on first appearance; records of
710	        # different tenants may interleave. The serialized tenant is only an
711	        # internal key so distinct types (1 vs "1") stay separate chains while
712	        # the original value is reported back unchanged. The shared lease
713	        # pins the snapshot to a state wholly before or after any append.
714	        return self._verify_all_snapshot(self._read_snapshot())

716	    def export_tenant(self, tenant):
717	        # Offline, single-tenant migration export. Returns UTF-8 bytes only:
718	        # it never creates, mutates or deletes any path and never touches the
719	        # network. The tenant crosses the same standard-JSON input boundary as
720	        # append/verify, and, like verify, it is checked before any history is
721	        # read, so an illegal value raises ValueError without a single byte
722	        # being read or created.
723	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
724	        # One shared-lease snapshot pins the whole export to a state wholly
725	        # before or after some append: a concurrent writer can never land in
726	        # the middle of it. Nothing is assembled into a result until the exact
727	        # scan verify(tenant) runs has cleared the complete snapshot, so a
728	        # corrupt source raises AuditChainStateError instead of returning the
729	        # verified prefix. A missing or empty file is a legitimate empty
730	        # snapshot and yields b"".
731	        data = self._read_snapshot()
732	        lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
733	        try:
734	            self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
735	        except _Broken as b:
736	            seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
737	            raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
738	        # The full snapshot is valid for this tenant; only now collect its
739	        # records in physical order, dropping every interleaved tenant. Each
740	        # record is re-emitted with the exact serialization and newline rule
741	        # append uses, so the bytes a caller drops at a new JSONL path verify
742	        # offline with unchanged seq/prev/hash semantics; distinct JSON tenant
743	        # identities never share an export.
744	        key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
745	        chunks = []
746	        for raw in lines:
747	            item = _strict_loads(raw)
748	            if self._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) == key:
749	                chunks.append(
750	                    (json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
751	                    .encode("utf-8")
752	                )
753	        return b"".join(chunks)

755	    def import_tenant(self, tenant, data):

757	        # (or any strictly valid single-tenant JSONL history) onto this log
758	        # without a network or remote anchor. The records keep their original
759	        # tenant/seq/event/prev/hash values verbatim -- nothing is renumbered
760	        # or recomputed -- so verify/verify_all/verify_bytes/export_tenant

762	        #
763	        # Boundary first, exactly as every other entry point orders it: the
764	        # tenant crosses the standard-JSON boundary and data must be bytes,
765	        # both before any lease is taken, any history is read or the path is
766	        # probed, so an illegal call raises ValueError regardless of target
767	        # state or contention and creates nothing. Empty bytes are a no-op
768	        # after that validation: no file is created, no history is read and
769	        # no byte changes.
770	        _validate_json_value(tenant)

772	            raise ValueError(f"data must be bytes, got {type(data).__name__}")

774	            return []

776	        # touched: strict UTF-8 JSONL, this exact canonical tenant identity on
777	        # every physical line, seq starting at 1 with prev ZERO and each
778	        # digest matching. A chain defect raises AuditChainStateError --
779	        # reason missing/sequence/digest, with tenant, seq and physical line
780	        # filled as append fills them; a record of any other tenant identity
781	        # violates the single-tenant input contract and raises ValueError.
782	        # Either kind reaches the caller before a target-side check can.

784	        try:
785	            records = self._scan_import(tenant, lines, bad_line)

788	                f"import data must contain only tenant {tenant!r}; "

791	        except _Broken as b:
792	            seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
793	            raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None

797	            # competing writers serialize wholly before or after it. A corrupt

799	            # priority over the emptiness assertion; a target that already
800	            # holds a record for this tenant is a conflict -- an import can

803	            # actual_*. Other tenants' valid records may already be present.
804	            target = f.read()

808	            except _Broken as b:

811	            if count != 0:
812	                raise AuditChainConflictError(
813	                    tenant, 0, ZERO, count, head
814	                )

816	            # re-serialized with the exact rule append/export use. The first

818	            # empty target chain regardless of the other tenants interleaved
819	            # on disk; seqs and hashes stay exactly the validated ones.
820	            chunks = [
821	                json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
822	                for item in records
823	            ]
824	            prefix = b"" if (not target or target.endswith(b"\n")) else b"\n"
825	            f.write(prefix + "".join(chunks).encode("utf-8"))

828	    def read_tenant(self, tenant, start_seq=1, page_size=None):

830	        # (each carrying exactly the tenant/seq/event/prev/hash fields with
831	        # their on-disk values) ordered by ascending seq; records of other
832	        # tenants may interleave on disk but never appear here or move the
833	        # page boundaries, since seqs are the target tenant's own 1..count.
834	        #
835	        # Every input crosses its boundary before any byte is read: the tenant
836	        # uses the same standard-JSON rule as append/verify/export, and
837	        # start_seq/page_size must be unambiguous positive integers (bool is
838	        # rejected even though it subclasses int; floats and other types are
839	        # too), with page_size additionally allowed to be None. A rejected
840	        # call reads nothing and, via the read-only snapshot below, can never
841	        # create or alter the log.
842	        _validate_json_value(tenant)
843	        if isinstance(start_seq, bool) or not isinstance(start_seq, int) \
844	                or start_seq < 1:
845	            raise ValueError(
846	                f"start_seq must be a positive integer, got {start_seq!r}"
847	            )
848	        if page_size is not None and (
849	            isinstance(page_size, bool) or not isinstance(page_size, int)
850	            or page_size < 1
851	        ):
852	            raise ValueError(
853	                "page_size must be a positive integer or None, got "
854	                f"{page_size!r}"
855	            )
856	        # One shared-lease snapshot, exactly as verify/export use: the result
857	        # is the full tenant history either wholly before or wholly after any
858	        # concurrent append, never a torn page. A missing path or an unknown
859	        # tenant is simply an empty chain and yields [].
860	        data = self._read_snapshot()
861	        lines, bad_line = self._decode_lines(data)
862	        try:
863	            # The whole tenant history -- first record through chain tail --
864	            # must verify with the exact JSON identity, sequence and digest
865	            # rules of verify before a single record is surfaced. Slicing
866	            # happens only after this, so a broken chain raises
867	            # AuditChainStateError (same tenant/seq/reason/line location as
868	            # verify/append/export) even when the requested page lies entirely
869	            # before the damage; no verified prefix is ever returned.
870	            self._scan(tenant, lines, bad_line)
871	        except _Broken as b:
872	            seq = b.at if b.at is not None else b.expect
873	            raise AuditChainStateError(tenant, seq, b.reason, b.line) from None
874	        # Snapshot proven valid: collect the target tenant in physical order
875	        # (identical to seq order for that tenant), then take the page purely
876	        # in memory. A start past the current count or a short tail page just
877	        # yields the available suffix, possibly [], rather than an error.
878	        key = self._tenant_key(tenant)
879	        records = []
880	        for raw in lines:
881	            item = _strict_loads(raw)
882	            if self._tenant_key(item["tenant"]) == key:
883	                records.append(item)
884	        lo = start_seq - 1
885	        if page_size is None:
886	            return records[lo:]
887	        return records[lo:lo + page_size]

893	        # (file snapshot) and verify_bytes (caller snapshot).

915	        # and other types are too). Both raise before the file is opened, so

925	    def verify_bytes(self, data, tenant, expected_count=None):
926	        # Pure in-memory, offline entry point. The caller hands over the raw
